Meanwhile, the changes in `SubWorkflowActionExecutor.java` ensure that the sub-workflow can now properly inject its configuration, allowing it to override properties defined in the parent workflow.

The updates in `TestSubWorkflowActionExecutor.java` serve to validate these changes, ensuring that the new behavior works as intended and that the sub-workflow can indeed override parent properties. injectInline(eConf.getChild("configuration", ns), subWorkflowConf);
```java
Configuration parentConf = new XConfiguration(new StringReader(context.getWorkflow().getConf()));
```

The bug occurs because the `injectInline` method is called before the parent workflow's configuration (`parentConf`) is read. This results in the inline configuration from the parent workflow being injected into the sub-workflow configuration (`subWorkflowConf`) before the parent configuration properties can be properly applied, preventing the sub-workflow from overriding any properties defined in the parent workflow XML.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
Configuration parentConf = new XConfiguration(new StringReader(context.getWorkflow().getConf()));
injectInline(eConf.getChild("configuration", ns), subWorkflowConf);
```
Reason:
The fix involves reordering the code so that the parent workflow's configuration is read and stored in `parentConf` before calling `injectInline`. This ensures that the sub-workflow configuration can correctly override any properties defined in the parent workflow, as the parent configuration is now available and applied first.
